mssql-rs.reason: At mssql-rs revision 3adfb4a4a099df5f10c9baa3934157750522b944, 568 non-NULL numeric/text-to-interval cases return HYC00 (Target type not yet implemented) instead of the required conversion or input-specific diagnostic. The 12 NULL interval cases pass and remain enabled. These exact cases pass with Microsoft ODBC Driver 18.6 on the same SQL Server 2022 instance.

All eight character-to-SQL_C_NUMERIC cases return HYC00 for valid input 42 and recovery input 1. Expected SQL_SUCCESS and a correctly populated SQL_NUMERIC_STRUCT. Reproduced under ODBC 3.0/3.8 with varchar/nvarchar and SQLGetData/SQLBindCol. Driver 18.6 passes these cases.

Input 1e-999 retrieved as SQL_C_DOUBLE succeeds with no diagnostic in the Rust driver; the reference cases require SQL_ERROR with 22003. Driver 18.6 reports the expected range error. Investigate Linux numeric underflow handling across varchar/nvarchar, both retrieval APIs, and ODBC versions.

For an empty varchar/nvarchar retrieved as SQL_C_SLONG, Driver 18.6 succeeds with indicator 0 and leaves the destination untouched; mssql-rs returns SQL_ERROR/22018. This is a reference-driver compatibility difference, not yet classified as a Rust conformance defect. Decide intended behavior before reenabling the eight exact parity cases.

For blank-only nvarchar retrieved as SQL_C_SLONG, mssql-rs returns 22018 while Driver 18.6 reports HY000. Both reject the value. This may be a deliberate diagnostic-policy difference rather than a conformance defect; review before reenabling four exact parity cases.

For nvarchar input -.0 retrieved as SQL_C_DOUBLE, mssql-rs succeeds while Driver 18.6 returns SQL_ERROR/22018. This appears to be a reference-driver parsing quirk, not a confirmed Rust defect. Decide the compatibility contract before reenabling four exact cases; narrow-character counterparts remain enabled.
